description.narrative: I korthet syftar projektet att främja inkluderande, klimatsmart ekonomisk utveckling i mejerisektorn med fokus på aktörer med bristande resurser och möjligheter, särskilt kvinnor och ungdomar, längs med värdekedjan för mejeriprodukter

In brief, the aim of the project is to to enable inclusive, climate-smart economic development in the dairy sector, with an emphasis on resource-poor, opportunity-constrained stakeholders, particularly women and youth, across the dairy value chain.

The DNA-BILD's overall objective is to contribute to transform Tanzania's dairy industry by creating vibrant ecosystems of farmer-allied and environmentally sustainable enterprises that improve nutrition, enhance livelihoods, and stimulate inclusive economic growth. The theory of change sets farmer-allied enterprises (FAEs), thus small-medium enterprises with strong links to farmers, to achieve long-term growth and to sustainably scale the benefits both upstream to farmers and farmer livelihoods, and downstream to improve nutrition of consumers. The enterprises are positioned to strategically and intentionally supply and/or source from smallholder farmers in a way that strengthens their capacity, improves their productivity, and enhances their livelihoods, resiliency, and adaptation to climate change. This, in turn, will enable the production of affordable, locally produced dairy products improving the consumption of high quality nutritious and safely processed dairy. Furthermore, the project DNA-BILD will build on the learnings, expertise and working methods of the Dairy Nourishes Africa (DNA) consortium and expands the initiatives outreach to underserved populations, particularly women and youth, and enhances programming for climate mitigation and resilience.

title.narrative: Amendment to the grant agreeemnt on diary nourishes Africa building inclusive livelihoods(DNA-BILD) between the Swedish International Development Cooperation Agency , Sida and Land O'lakes Venture 37

description.narrative:
The results monitoring is based on the agreed 4 implementation pillars. Below some examples of the results achieved for each pillar.
PILLAR 1: Grow consumer demand: DNA-BILD aimed to reach 10,000 dairy consumers through various tailored activities. This target was already reached by 234% in 2023, therefore the Embassy assessing the continuous growth in demand as new achievement milestone.
PILLAR 2: Drive enterprises to their full potential: Supporting medium and small-scale Farmer-Allied Enterprises (FAEs) aim to improve a demand pull that promotes commercialization of farming and improvement of livelihood for greater number of smallholder farmers. The intervention by cooperation partner is building capacity of FAEs though business development technical training to improve their business management skills. In addition, part of the contribution (totaling over USD 88,000) was used to create small challenge find grants. A qualifying enterprise received a grant of no more than $5,000 USD to be used to purchase processing or storage equipment for their businesses. The Dairy Challenge Fund participants also were required to raise the matching capital whereby over $60,000 USD was co-invested. Based on the findings from the annual survey conducted in February 2025, the average annual sales of the 16 dairy processors surveyed was $133,593, representing a 73% increase from sales of their first 6 months of project participation.
PILLAR 3: Increase farmer productivity: The ultimate objective under this pillar is increase in income of the dairy farmers. The increase in income is expected to be a result of contribution supported by supported smallholder dairy farmers gaining practical skills on production enhancing technologies including cow housing, cow feed rationing and feeding, disease control and animal health management, improved cattle genetics, and milk handling and hygiene as well as business skills. This is achieved by project intervention in two areas: the volume of milk produced per cow, per day and the sale prices of produced milk (during the rainy and dry seasons). The main contributing factors the project interventions are targeting in order to achieve the high daily milk yields per day per cow: feeding and husbandry. It is reported that the project intervention has been in climate smart nutritious feeds and fodder production and improved feed storage technologies. This includes silage and hay making, planting of multipurpose trees etc.
Based on the partners farmer survey during early 2025, cow productivity was maintained at 8.9 liters per cow, per day, on average. This is 1.6 liters above the baseline value of 7.3 liters per cow, per day. Analysis of the survey revealed that the average annual income for smallholder dairy farmers supported by DNA-BILD is USD $1,492. This reflects a 60.1% increase from the baseline figure of $931 per year. This means that the DNA-BILD overachieved the life of project target of $1,125 USD per year by 133%. Farmers interviewed through focus group discussions attributed to growth in annual farmer income can be attributed to application of improved practices and increase in productivity.
The project has started the promotion of artificial insemination for high yielding cows, improved milk handling and hygiene.
Pillar 4: Strengthen the operating environment: Regarding this pillar the report mainly highlights the DNA-BILD hosted the fourth and final stakeholder meeting on 25 June 2025 as project closeout event. It is reported that 75 stakeholders from representatives of smallholder dairy farmers, FAEs, local, regional, and district government officials, extension officers, Artificial Insemination technicians, Ministry of Livestock and Fisheries officials, and Tanzania Dairy Board representatives. The event was used by V37 to share the highlights of project results, outcomes, and impacts.
